en: The Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī Sūtra, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was on the summit of Mount Potalaka, [contemplating] Avalokiteśvara...
The place where the palace of sound is situated is a mountain range abounding in śāla trees, tamāla trees,
campaka flower trees, atimuktaka flower trees, and others.
Furthermore, there were various kinds of immeasurable and boundless trees made of diverse jewels,
which adorned the surroundings.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of eight thousand bhikṣus.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable Śuddhāvāsa devas,
surrounded on all sides by immeasurable hundreds of thousands;
their names were the hosts of Īśvara devas and the hosts of Maheśvara devas.
Furthermore, there were several Great Brahma Kings and various devaputras who requested the Buddha to preach the Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Thereupon, from within the great assembly gathered like the ocean,
[a certain being] rose from his seat, adjusted his robes,
bared his right shoulder, and placed his right knee upon the ground.
With palms joined toward the Buddha, his face radiant and serene,
he opened his countenance with a smile and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, regarding the mantra for those possessed of mind..."
It is named the King of Amoghapāśa.
Since I first gave rise to the bodhicitta in the distant past,
ninety-one kalpas have passed.
In that kalpa, there was a world named Avalokita.
Within that buddha-field, there was another Buddha named Lokendrarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
However, out of compassion for me, that Tathāgata taught this heart-mantra.
At that time, I received and maintained it from that Blessed One without forgetting;
by the power of this, [I have attained this state].
From that time forth, he has constantly preached the Dharma and transformed countless, boundless hundreds of thousands of great celestial hosts of Maheśvaras,
as well as the kings of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens and their innumerable sons.
"May they be directed toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
World-Honored One, having received this dhāraṇī from that Buddha,
I immediately attained ten thousand samādhis, such as the 'Unforgetting Wisdom' and the 'Supreme Adornment.'"
World-Honored One, wherever this heart-mantra exists,
one should know that there are great hosts of devas, namely Maheśvara and Maheśāna.
The Great Brahmā, Brahmā, and twelve thousand others shall guard, protect, and defend it.
Wherever the World-Honored One may be, wherever this mantra resides,
one should regard that place as a stūpa.
World-Honored One, wherever this heart-mantra exists,
one should know for certain that those people have already made offerings to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Buddhas and have planted roots of goodness.
World-Honored One, if there should be another person who hears this mantra of non-emptiness,
it should be known that such a person,
regarding others in the past, [has committed no transgressions].
Committing various defilements and evils, they perform all manner of unrighteous acts;
slandering their teachers and slandering the True Dharma,
they will surely fall into the Avīci Hell in a future life.
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and others completely abandon [such people].
Thereafter, those individuals give rise to a mind of regret and remorse, and no longer commit evil deeds.
If that person can fast for one day and one night and recite this heart-mantra,
their grave offenses will be experienced lightly in the present life;
or they may suffer from a feverish illness for a single day.
Or again, after two days, or three days, or four days,
or even seven days, they may contract a feverish illness,
or experience eye pain, or suffer from earache.
Or there may be pain in the lips and teeth, or pain in the tongue and palate;
or again, pain in the heart, or pain in the abdomen;
or pain in the knees, or pain in the flanks, the waist, the spine, and the ribs.
Some suffer from pain in the limbs and joints; some contract hemorrhoids;
some experience obstructions in the passage of feces or urine, or suffer from diarrhea;
others suffer afflictions of the hands, feet, or head.
They may suffer from pain, or afflictions such as sores, scabies, white leprosy, major leprosy, sweet sores, blistering sores, *fanhua* sores, malignant toxic sores, or "monthly-eating" sores.
Or they may contract epilepsy, various demonic illnesses, and the like.
Or they may encounter curses and various utterances on the wilderness paths;
or what was done for another may instead fall upon them,
or what was done for oneself may instead befall others.
Or they may be imprisoned and confined in a jail; or they may be beaten by others, or killed by others;
or they may be subjected to threats, verbal abuse, insults, and humiliation, or slandered.
World-Honored One, I shall now speak briefly:
whether one encounters the pressing afflictions of the actions of body, speech, and mind,
or whether one experiences bad dreams at night.
Because they experience the results in the present life, those evil karmas are entirely eliminated;
how much more so for pure sentient beings who possess right faith and right practice— for it is impossible that their sins would not be extinguished.
World-Honored One, if there are members of the fourfold assembly who,
with a deceitful and crooked mind, hear this dhāraṇī,
or further recite it, or further uphold it;
Whether reciting it constantly day and night or explaining it for others, one should instruct them to listen;
even before animals, one should recite this heart-mantra so that they may hear it with their ears.
Furthermore, one is able to speak these vajra-words and so forth as mental recitations from one's own mind. What are these vajra-words?
They are what is called "not abandoning anything."
All non-discrimination is this.
All unconditioned phenomena are this.
All that does not arrive late is this.
All non-doing is this. All non-attachment is this.
The mind of universal equanimity is this.
All things are non-arrival; this is it.
All things are non-abandonment; this is it.
All things are non-separation from the five aggregates; this is it.
By such means, one must practice the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*).
Then, those Buddhas of the ten directions, numbering a full thousand, will appear before one.
Those Buddhas shall instruct this person in repentance to eliminate their transgressions.
World-Honored One, I have now spoken briefly.
If there should be anyone who writes this heart-mantra on bamboo or silk, and receives, maintains, and pays homage to it.
There are such immeasurable and boundless accumulations of merit as these.
World-Honored One, I have now briefly described them.
Those who hear this mantra should not give rise to contention.
World-Honored One, if a person who is engaged in a dispute with another hears this dhāraṇī—
whether out of fear for their family, to protect the feelings of others,
or due to playful jesting— and hears this dhāraṇī;
World-Honored One, those people should reflect thus:
"That my ear-faculty hears this mantra is due to the majestic spiritual power of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, and not by my own power."
World-Honored One, it is as if there were a person who takes sandalwood incense, or takes camphor incense,
or takes musk and various other such fragrances.
Having finished speaking words of slander, defamation, and abuse,
he then again smeared that incense upon his body.
However, that sandalwood, up to and including the musk, does not form such a thought:
"That person slanders me, reviles me, or insults me.
How could it ever have such a mind?
"Does my fragrance belong to me and not to him? That is impossible.
World-Honored One, it is simply that he himself possesses the nature of fragrance; he does not abandon his own inherent nature."
"So it is, so it is. World-Honored One,
if there should be anyone who reviles or insults this heart-mantra of mine,"
Or again, they may speak with slander as described above;
yet with a deceitful mind, they pay homage and show respect to the World-Honored One.
Those deceitful sentient beings, in future ages, [will suffer...]
Regarding all roots of goodness, they can serve as the cause for Buddhahood.
In every birth and in every place, they are never separated from the fragrance of the accumulation of merit achieved through precepts, meditative concentration, and superior wisdom.
In future ages, they will be able to maintain the fragrance of the precepts.
World-Honored One, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family,
or a bhikṣu, bhikṣuṇī, upāsaka, or upāsikā,
or any other persons, for the sake of this heart-mantra—
On the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of the month,
one should fast for one day and one night without eating,
maintaining the prohibitive precepts with the body and practicing diligence with the mind.
Recite this heart mantra seven times during the day and again seven times at night. Having recited it,
do not think of other matters and do not converse with others.
World-Honored One, that person shall obtain twenty kinds of merit in the present life.
What are these twenty kinds of merit?
First, no illnesses or pains shall afflict their body.
First, although they may suffer from illness or pain, by the power of their meritorious karma, they will quickly recover.
Second, their bodies will be subtle, supple, and radiant, such that many people will love and respect them.
Third, their faculties will be well-disciplined.
Fourth, one will obtain great wealth and treasures, and whatever is sought will be fulfilled according to one's wishes, without being plundered by others.
Fifth, fire cannot burn them.
Sixth, water cannot sweep them away.
Seventh, the king cannot seize it;
whatever karma one creates will always result in good fortune and prosperity.
Eighth, destructive hail will not cause harm, and evil dragons will withdraw their venom.
Ninth, one will not suffer from droughts nor fear malignant winds or torrential rains.
Tenth, if someone’s crops are being devoured by insects,
one should take sand, ashes, or water and recite the mantra over them seven times at will.
One binds the boundaries of the eight directions, universally binding all directions above and below.
All terrors and all venomous insects shall be immediately extinguished.
Eleventh, all evil spirits that suck the vital essence from people [shall likewise be eliminated].
Or if they become husband and wife in a dream,
even if they desire to bewitch one another with malevolent magic, they cannot cause harm.
Twelfth, they will always obtain peace and happiness among all evil sentient beings.
One’s mind shall always be respectful and reverent, never abandoning this for even a moment.
Thirteenth, should any enemies give rise to malicious intent and come to seek retribution,
they shall naturally be extinguished.
Fourteenth, whenever there are wicked people who wish to cause him harm,
they are unable to do so and must depart of their own accord.
Fifteenth, all incantations and all sorcery [are rendered ineffective].
Sixteenth, they immediately restrain themselves and are unable to inflict harm.
Seventeenth, even when among a multitude, they are the most powerful.
Eighteenth, no afflictions are able to entangle or surround them.

Eighteenth: When amidst an enemy array where blades and weapons are inflicting harm, if one recites the mantra with single-minded concentration, no swords, staves, arrows, or shafts shall strike the body.
Nineteenth: All benevolent deities will constantly follow and protect one.
"Twentieth: in every birth and in every place, one shall always not be separated from loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
World-Honored One, if any person can receive and uphold such a heart-mantra, they shall obtain these twenty kinds of merit."
World-Honored One, there are further eight dharmas to be attained.
First, on the day of one's death, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara shall manifest before that person in the form of a bhikṣu.
Second, at the time of death, their minds will not be distracted and the four great elements will remain tranquil;
they will be free from all suffering and affliction that might otherwise beset their bodies.
Third, even when their illness is grave and terminal, there will be no leakage of impurities, such as foul-smelling excrement or urine.
Fourth, on the day of their death, they shall attain right mindfulness with minds free from confusion or error.
Fifth, on the day of their death, they shall not die with their faces turned downward.
Sixth, on the day of their death, they shall attain immeasurable eloquence.
Seventh, on the day of their death, if they wish to be born in whichever Buddha-land they desire, they will be reborn there according to their will.
Eighth, they will always encounter virtuous friends (kalyāṇamitra) and never be parted from them. Thus, these eight kinds of meritorious signs manifest before that person.
If there is anyone who can recite and maintain this mantra three times during each of the three periods of the day, three times per period,
they should abstain from alcohol, meat, and the five pungent herbs.
Then the merit thus obtained will increase day and night.
The Bodhisattva does not do this for his own sake;
rather, knowing the power of the mental nature of all sentient beings, he should explain it for their benefit.
Do not be stingy; do not be arrogant or envious.
Nor should you say, "I can do this for you, but you cannot. Why is that?
The Bodhisattva abandons the mind of envy;
for the sake of all sentient beings, he brings about great benefit,
attains bodhi, and enters the ranks of the Bodhisattvas.
That which is called "bodhi" is great wisdom;
that which is called "sentient beings" is skillful means.
These two dharmas exist for the sake of sentient beings and are thus attained.
World-Honored One, I pray that the Buddha will grant me leave to recite this heart-mantra.
I wish to expound it before the Tathāgata,
and also for the sake of all beings of the fourfold assembly.
For the sake of attaining peace and happiness, for the sake of attaining benefit,
and furthermore, for the sake of eliminating the transgressions of other sinful sentient beings,
the World-Honored One then addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"You, O pure being, have spoken this heart-mantra;
you should know that the Tathāgata rejoices in it at the proper time.
This is the heart-mantra."
In future ages, those sons and daughters of good family who practice the bodhisattva path should regard this heart-mantra as their father and mother.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Beholding the Honored One’s countenance, his eyes never for a moment leaving it,
he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, the Buddha has already granted me permission to recite this heart-mantra."
All bodhisattvas should pay homage to, revere,
and honor this dharma-gate of the perfection of liberation,
for the sake of the benefit and happiness of many beings.
Out of compassion for the multitude of beings,
and so that the worlds of gods and humans may attain worldly happiness,
I now prostrate to all Buddhas of the three times.
And to the assembly of Bodhisattvas, and the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas of the past, future, and present—
I now prostrate to all the noble ones who practice correctly and proceed toward the right path.
I now prostrate to the Greatly Wise Śāriputra.
I now prostrate to the World-Honored One Maitreya and the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
I now prostrate to our Original Teacher, the Tathāgata Amitābha.
I now prostrate to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One.
He then spoke this mantra:
*tadyathā | oṃ hūṃ | jvala jvala | cili cili | julu julu*.

16. Sarvasattvasamāśvāsaka 147. Namaḥ sute 148. Svāhā 149. This mantra is perfected as soon as it is recited.
Recite it one hundred and eight times during each of the three periods of the day;
this can eliminate the five heinous crimes and all karmic obstructions.
When burning aloeswood incense and wishing to establish a ritual boundary (*sīmābandha*), [recite as follows].
Alternatively, one may consecrate water, or consecrate ashes,
or consecrate mustard seeds, or consecrate four pieces of red sandalwood,
each seven times, and nail them into the four directions.
For all diseases of malarial fever and chills,
one should fashion a mantra-cord, recite it twenty-one times, and tie it around the neck;
immediately, all such ailments will be cured.
One may consecrate either ghee, oil, or water by reciting the mantra twenty-one times for each;
having thus consecrated them, one should consume them.
If one wishes to destroy the curses cast by others, [one should do so].
One should fashion an image of that person out of flour, clay, or wax,
and then cut it piece by piece with a blade of tempered steel.
If there is anyone who is terrified and wishes to protect their body,
they should fashion a mantra-cord and wear it upon themselves.
If there is anyone suffering from abdominal pain, [they should do the same].
Chanting the mantra over brine, one should drink it.
If someone has been afflicted by insect venom or bitten by a snake,
one should use the mantra to consecrate an ointment and apply it to them.
If anyone suffers from eye pain, take white thread and,
having consecrated it with mantras, tie it upon their ear. If anyone suffers from toothache, [take white thread and, having consecrated it with mantras, tie it upon their ear].
Recite the mantra over a *kāravīra* tree twenty-one times;
thereafter, chew it and rub it against one's teeth. This is for when one wishes to establish a great boundary (*mahā-sīmā*).
Take five-colored threads and recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Take four pieces of red sandalwood to serve as stakes; tie ropes to the stakes and wind them around them.
Drive them into the four corners, and thus a great boundary is established.
First, for one who wishes to protect their body from all places of fear and all causes for alarm,
they should carry a consecrated mantra-cord;
or they may sprinkle consecrated water upon themselves, or scatter consecrated ashes over them.
If one is possessed by a ghost, take five-colored threads and fashion them into a mantra-cord to wear or tie around the body.
For all those suffering from cold-fever or heat-fever ailments,
take white threads, recite the mantra twenty-one times over them, and fashion them into a cord to wear while traveling.
If one suffers from any kind of malignant ulcer,
take pippalī, pound it into a powder, mix it with honey,
and recite the mantra twenty-one times over it; then apply it as a paste upon the ulcer.
If anyone suffers from eye ailments,
they should take fragrant decoction or licorice decoction,
recite the mantra twenty-one times over it, and wash both eyes with it.
If anyone suffers from an ear ailment,
they should boil oil, recite the mantra twenty-one times over it, and pour it into the ear.
This applies to all disputes, all legal affairs, and all places of fear.
Recite the water-mantra twenty-one times and wash one's face.
If there is a great epidemic within the country,
or in a city, town, or village...
One should even turn one's home into a maṇḍala.
Smear the ground with cow dung and sprinkle it with fragrant water.
Place new, clean water jars in each of the four corners.
Place various kinds of flowers inside the vases;
further, scatter various kinds of flowers upon the site of the *maṇḍala*.
Take various kinds of food and drink and ensure they are all fragrant and delicious.
Furthermore, he spread various kinds of pure grass to establish the site of enlightenment (*maṇḍala*).
Upon it, he placed food along with various fruits and melons.
At each of the four corners, he fashioned lamp bowls out of flour.
One should prepare a wick from clean cloth and burn various exquisite incenses,
making offerings with the most excellent and superior ones.
The mantra-practitioner shall bathe with fragrant water and don fresh, clean garments.
Having spread a new and clean mat upon that seat and sat thereon, one should recite and maintain this dhāraṇī;
all calamities and transformations will then be immediately extinguished.
If there should be anyone who encounters a serious illness, [this shall likewise be applied].
Having consecrated the water in that vessel with mantras, one sprinkles it upon that person.
All those upon whom it is sprinkled shall immediately be freed from all epidemics,
malevolent spirits, and every place of fear.
If one sprinkles water [upon them], they will all be healed.
If someone has been subjected to the spells of others,
one should grind sandalwood and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times.
If one applies mud to the heart center, it will be immediately healed.
If one wishes to eliminate all karmic obstructions, as well as the five heinous crimes and the four grave offenses,
one should constantly recite [the mantra] without ceasing.
If there is an epidemic within a household,
or if various spirits are causing disturbances in the home,
one should take one hundred and eight lotus flowers.
Recite the mantra once over each lotus flower and cast them into the fire; they will immediately be cured.
If one wishes to take hold of the minds and intentions of all sentient beings:
One should take one hundred and eight pieces of sandalwood, each two inches long.
Recite the mantra over each piece once and cast it into the fire.
This is for treating all demonic illnesses and places of terror.

One should take *jaya* grass, *vijaya* grass, *nāgari* medicinal herb, *kandhanāgari* grass, *cillani* grass, *abhayaparni* grass, *indraparni* grass, *vālaka* (vetiveria), *tagara*, *cakra*, *mahācakra*, *visnu-kantaka*, *sumana*, and *sunanda* grass.
All these various herbs were pounded into a powder and finely sifted;
water was added to form pills the size of jujube fruits.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Whether worn upon the head or tied to the hand while walking,
no demonic illnesses or pestilences shall be able to cause harm.
If there are children afflicted by demonic diseases or pestilence, or those who are terrified in dangerous places,
one should take a pill and tie it beneath their throat.
If there are women with unattractive features who find it difficult to marry, or those suffering from various illnesses, [the same should be done].
Take this medicinal pill, mix it with water, and bathe;
immediately the inauspicious signs will be removed—this is most wonderful, most supreme, and accomplished at will without difficulty.
If there is a woman who does not give birth to a son, [she shall obtain one].
If one takes a single pill of this medicine and ties it around the neck, one will immediately give birth to a son.
It provides great protection against all terrors and fears.
Furthermore, for anyone afflicted by insects:
This medicine can also destroy them.
One who wears this medicine while traveling will not be burned by fire nor encounter other calamities.
Even if afflicted by malignant sores, [it shall heal them].
Whoever applies this medicine shall immediately be cured.
If anyone is oppressed by various evil deeds,
wearing this medicine shall cause them to be delivered from their hardships.
If there is anyone who wishes to eliminate evil winds and heavy rains,
they should recite the mantra over water twenty-one times and scatter it in the four directions;
the winds and rains will immediately be dispelled and cease.
If one encounters a great hailstorm,
take a branch from a tree and strike it from a distance while reciting this mantra;
even if this Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara has not been formally received or maintained.
Merely by reciting it, one can destroy all karmic obstructions;
all undertakings will be accomplished. If there is anyone who upholds this mantra, [all their goals shall be fulfilled].
That person shall weave a single white cotton cloth,
five feet wide and ten feet long, without cutting it.
Upon the warp and weft of that cloth, one must paint a single Buddha.
In the pigments, glue must not be used;
rather, one should mix them with incense and milk to paint the figures.
On the right side, one should paint an image of Avalokiteśvara.
His appearance was like that of the god Maheśvara;
the hair upon his head was entirely arranged in a conch-shell topknot,
and he wore a square floral crown.
On the shoulder, one should depict a black deer skin draped over the left shoulder;
the remaining parts of the body should be depicted with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments.
The painter shall be instructed to observe the eightfold fast (aṣṭāṅga-upavāsa) and must not consume mixed food.
Every day, one should bathe in scented water to purify oneself and put on clean garments.
The mantra-practitioner should place the image in a clean location and smear the ground before the image with cow dung.
The four sides are uniform, measuring sixteen feet in length and breadth.
Within the ritual enclosure, scatter pure white flowers and place eight water jars, each with a capacity of one *dou*.
He had them all thoroughly cleansed and filled with fragrant water;
he further placed various kinds of flowers inside the vases and set pure grasses upon the eight seats made of grass.
Having established these in the eight directions, one prepares eight portions of food and places them upon their grass seats.
Thereafter, one further prepares sixty-four portions of food,
each consisting of various kinds of diverse and excellent delicacies.
All other miscellaneous food items were prepared and displayed on a vast scale;
with the sole exception of the five pungent roots,
alcohol, and meat, everything else that could possibly be obtained was provided in full.
If one wishes to perform the recitation of mantras,
one should abstain from food for three days and three nights and burn aloeswood incense.
The practitioner of the mantra should bathe three times a day with water scented with exquisite fragrances.
Whenever one voids urine or excrement, one must bathe.
If one is unable to do so for three days and three nights,
one should simply fast for one day and one night.
One should consume three kinds of white foods— milk, curd, and non-glutinous rice—
and having knelt for a long time before that image to present food and drink,
one should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
At that time, while the practitioner was before the image,
they immediately saw their own body emit a great radiance like a blazing flame.
Having seen this for themselves, they gave rise to great joy.
Even unto the point where Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva manifests his own body in person;
he grants all their heart's desires according to their wishes.
If they wish to become invisible, [he grants this as well].
One should take realgar or mineral antimony,
pound it until it is a fine powder, and sift it.
Before the image, one should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
By applying it to the eyes, one immediately attains invisibility,
even to the point of soaring through the air.
Furthermore, one attains a samādhi named "Adorned with the Vision of Non-empty Wisdom."
Having performed these rites,
whatever one subsequently undertakes shall all be accomplished.
This dhāraṇī method I have now fully explained.
At that time, when the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
the various devaputras of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, and Mahābrahmā, the lord of the Sahā world, [all paid homage].
The assembly of bodhisattvas, the assembly of śrāvakas, and all the great multitude of people,
having heard Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva speak this sutra before the Buddha,
were all filled with great joy and practiced it accordingly.
The Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī Sūtra
